cells.tense: You are standing in the middle of what you have carried, and you still have somewhere to put your feet.
cells.ask: Look at what is still up because you kept it up, name two things you did, and keep going. There is no grade after that.
cells.core: You are still following what you set out for. It has been a long road, and holding on has not turned you to stone. You know the difference now between force and staying put. You can feel in yourself which one you are using, and it does not cost you the way hurry does. The picture of this working is quieter than most people imagine. You keep going without making a scene, and your hands stay open while you do it. You are allowed to stop asking whether that is enough. It is your day and your steady hands, and the ground under you holds because you have not moved off it. The one cost is that staying can look like staying silent. It does not have to. What you keep steady is still here because you stayed with it.
cells.sheetLine: Still here, still steady, not stiff — that is the whole of it.
cells.verb: continuing to follow what you first hoped for, after everything that has built up around it
cells.place: where you hold what has to be held, without going stiff or giving out

cells.tense: You are leaning into a load that has not been handed to you yet, bracing for a weight you cannot see.
cells.ask: Pick one worry about tomorrow and do nothing about it until tomorrow. Put down what you picked up in advance and let the day hold its own weight.
cells.core: You are running a load that has not arrived. The strength that should keep you steady is spending itself on what might land next month, or next week, or in a conversation nobody has started yet. You rehearse the bracing before there is anything to brace against. The picture of this working is simple. You keep going, and the going does not need you to stand under tomorrow's rain today. That is where your strength has been leaking. The way back is not a harder grip. It is leaving one thing unguarded — letting a question stay open, letting a person arrive with their own answer, letting the day come to you instead of meeting it halfway. When you stop carrying ahead of time, what is yours to carry gets a chance to show itself.

cells.tense: There was a point where you stopped offering to carry, and you are still standing at that door as if it had not closed behind you.
cells.ask: Put your hands on one real task today — the dish, the bill, the small fix — and let that be enough without asking it to prove anything.
cells.core: You hold less than you used to. What you have is still yours, but it has gone quiet because you stopped giving it anything to do. The picture of this working is not heroic. It is smaller than before. You pick up one thing that needs doing, you do it, and you let that count. What is missing is not effort. Pushing harder will not fill what has gone quiet. What fills it is care with a shape to it, tending something that actually grows. Water the small thing in front of you, the plant or the bill or the person who needs a call, and let that be the whole of it. Do that and what you thought you lost starts moving again on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold more than you are holding. That door is behind you.

cells.tense: You are already keeping the thing upright, and you are telling people it is simply how things are.
cells.ask: Claim one thing you keep steady as yours. Say it out loud to someone: this stays standing because of what you do. Once, plainly.
cells.core: You are the reason a few things are still upright. Not because you make a scene about it, but because you keep showing up and doing the steady work that keeps them there. What you describe as just getting on is what holds them. The picture of this working is not a bigger grip. It is exactly what you already do, named. You are not asked to announce anything. Just to own one piece of it — one thing that stays put because of your hands on it — and to let someone else hear you say so. When that gets named, something loosens. What you have been doing under a different label becomes yours to put down, or to pick up with both hands. Either way, you decide.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding it up. You have been calling it nothing.
